scope: Eight Rust backend manuscripts and their executable examples.
review_type: Author editorial and factual pass; no independent human review is claimed.
publication: All eight approved after the two review passes: draft:false, reviewed:true, valid reviewedHash, and publication dates from October 26 through November 1, 2026.
language: Short sentences and familiar words for non-native English readers. Different problems and explanations give the articles their voice; deliberate mistakes and invented personal incidents are excluded.

evidence.result: All eleven backend tests passed. The job then required the generated lockfile and Rust formatting to be committed. These were retrieved from the CI artifact.
evidence.current_revision: See the required Content safety checks on https://github.com/mehdiakiki/mehdi-cz/pull/12.
evidence.manuscript_result: All eight exact-excerpt checks, the site safety suite, the production build, private rendering, and all eleven backend tests passed. The final gate required committing the preserved article and JSON formatting. Those changes were applied before the final verification run.
limits: The router and two-replica tests use HTTP request values in-process, not two deployed servers.
The shutdown tests use an actual Linux child process, TCP HTTP, and SIGTERM; Kubernetes and external load-balancer drain are not tested.
Tracing captures in-process ancestry around a real PostgreSQL query; OTLP export and cross-service propagation are not configured.
Migration tests use old and new SQL query functions; they do not launch separate application binaries or measure production DDL locks.
The session fixture uses synthetic bearer tokens and independent pools; browser login, cookies, CSRF, and lagging replicas remain outside scope.
Upload recovery uses real files and PostgreSQL state after successful storage. It does not test an HTTP upload stream, a process crash, S3 multipart APIs, or power-loss durability.
The lease generation check protects an effect in the same PostgreSQL statement. External effects need their own protocol.

article_notes.finding: A strict extractor and a Result-wrapped extractor have different handler entry behaviour. The text explains that change and retains 400, 422, and 415 rather than accepting any failure.
article_notes.release_check: Choose the final public error schema and check endpoint-specific body limits when adapting the fixture.

article_notes.finding: The virtual-clock results are ordering evidence, not benchmark timings. The deadline stops at response creation and does not establish a streamed-body deadline.
article_notes.release_check: Keep the timer scope and synthetic identity lookup clear.

article_notes.finding: The test signals a process only after a work request starts. Both successful drain and a finite failure boundary are observed.
article_notes.release_check: Do not turn the local readiness flag into a claim that an actual load balancer drained traffic.

article_notes.finding: Both HTTP paths return a correct result; the assertion checks the missing parent relationship directly. The current-thread subscriber is a fixture arrangement.
article_notes.release_check: Keep production subscriber initialization and cross-service export separate from the demonstrated spawn boundary.

article_notes.finding: The test makes an old writer stale a non-null backfill, then checks the precise 23502 failure after enforcement. The text closes the old-writer rollback window before switching authority.
article_notes.release_check: No zero-downtime or safe production batch-size claim is made by the small table.

article_notes.finding: Independent pools observe committed logout. The manuscript separates later lookups from an identity already resolved before revocation.
article_notes.release_check: Maintain the distinction between a session-store example and complete browser authentication.

article_notes.finding: Publication and cancellation compete through conditional state changes; a repeated missing-file delete can complete cleanup. Ready files are retained.
article_notes.release_check: The source is a local coordinator lab. Test a chosen remote storage adapter and the uncertain storage-acknowledgement boundary before expanding the promise.

article_notes.finding: A forced two-generation history checks the final stored effect. Epoch checks share a statement with the effect rather than preceding a separate unprotected write.
article_notes.release_check: Do not present the lease or generation as permission to perform an arbitrary external effect.

before_publication: Require green Content safety checks on the final scheduled revision.
Inspect rendered review copies and confirm only due articles have production routes and search entries.
Merge the approved PR, then verify the production deployment and the existing hourly due-publication check.

review_waves.purpose: Check technical claims against primary documentation and enrich the examples. These are author review passes, not a claim of independent human review.

articles.changes: Add a tested 413 response and an explicit endpoint body limit; distinguish default extractor limits from a global stream limit.
Compare ServiceBuilder with repeated Router.layer calls using the same paused-clock requests.
Explain why a shell entrypoint and testing Ctrl+C can hide a missing SIGTERM path.
Explain instrument macro argument capture and how skip_all plus explicit safe fields avoids accidental secret logging.
Show a tested update path which writes both columns; explain null-safe comparison and the rollout read/write phases.
Check expired and independent active sessions, and a closed store returning 503; fix an awkward sentence about a previously resolved identity.
Show cancellation SQL and a state table; explain why an unknown storage outcome must not be treated as a completed cleanup.
Add guarded lease renewal and checks for expired, stale, current, and completed owners; clarify that lease expiry is checked at the update, not promised at commit time.
